name: Daylight hours in New York City
notes: Computed, no download; 40.7128N 74.0060W, -0.833 deg solar altitude; checked against published NYC solstice day lengths to within 3 minutes. Deterministic annual cycle, so any lead-lag hit is a seasonality-in-returns finding, not a forecast. Kamstra, Kramer & Levi (2003, AER) seasonal-affective-disorder effect; they also stress the change in daylight around the equinoxes, so the test may want diff here.

name: Days since the last new moon at the US close
notes: Sawtooth: resets at each new moon (a linear correlation treats day 29 and day 0 as far apart). Computed, no download: Meeus (1998) Astronomical Algorithms ch. 48-49; new-moon instants validated against published times to within minutes. Evaluated at 16:00 New York time each calendar day (incl. weekends). Deterministic and known years in advance, hence known_after_days 0. Lunar-cycle 'moonstruck' effect: Yuan, Zheng & Zhu (2006) found lower returns around full moons. Near-placebo: a lead-lag hit at a non-29.5-day offset is noise.

name: Kamstra-Kramer-Levi SAD variable for New York
units: hours (night length minus 12, fall and winter only)
notes: KKL (2003) SAD_t = night hours - 12 for dates 21 Sep-20 Mar, 0 otherwise, at New York. Deterministic seasonal series; see astro_daylight_nyc.

name: SF Fed Daily News Sentiment Index
source: Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco
units: sentiment score (day fixed effects; higher = more positive)
notes: Shapiro, Sudhof & Wilson (2022) lexical sentiment of economics articles in 24 US newspapers. The published series is a TRAILING weighted average with geometrically declining weights (lag-1 autocorrelation 0.997), so it is smooth: transform diff; the daily change mostly reflects the newest articles. No look-ahead from the smoothing (trailing). Updated weekly (Mondays, through the previous Sunday), so a value can wait up to a week: known_after_days 8. Daily values are revised as the article sample updates, and the whole series was recomputed from Factiva in April 2021, so stored values differ from what was public at the time. Stands in for GDELT news tone, which was skipped.

name: US civilian noninstitutional population aged 16+ (monthly)
notes: Date = first day of the reference month (FRED convention); known_after_days counted from that date. Released in the BLS Employment Situation, usually the first Friday of the next month (about 33-40 days after the date); 42 is a conservative bound for normal months (shutdown delays: Sep 2013, Sep 2025). Oct 2025 is missing (no CPS during the 2025 shutdown). CPS population controls are introduced each January WITHOUT revising earlier months, so logdiff shows level breaks every January (e.g. Jan 2000, 2012, 2022, 2024, 2025, 2026); these are methodology steps, not population moves. Usable only at 21/63-day move lengths.

name: US resident population incl. armed forces overseas (monthly)
notes: Date = first day of the reference month (FRED convention); known_after_days counted from that date. Published in BEA Personal Income and Outlays about 4 weeks after month end, i.e. about 56-60 days after the date; 65 is a conservative bound for normal months (government shutdowns delayed it, e.g. Sep 2025 data appeared in Dec 2025). Very smooth (interpolated from Census estimates) and revised at every Census vintage and intercensal update; values are the latest revision, not what was known at the time. Usable only at 21/63-day move lengths.

name: World population (annual, mid-year)

name: Planetary geomagnetic Ap index (daily)
units: Ap index (unitless; x2 nT at 50 deg geomagnetic latitude)
notes: Daily mean of the eight 3-hour ap values. Heavily right-skewed (storm days 30-400). Krivelyova & Robotti (2003) found lower US returns in the days after geomagnetic storms. GFZ file mixes definitive and preliminary values: Kp/Ap definitive through about 2026-09-30, nowcast after (nowcast values are replaced by definitive ones, usually within a month; differences are small). Values stored are the definitive ones a trader would only have seen as nowcasts. UT days.

name: F10.7 solar radio flux, observed (daily)
units: solar flux units (1e-22 W m^-2 Hz^-1)
notes: Local-noon (about 20 UT) observed flux at Penticton; follows the 11-year solar cycle. Solar-activity series: a placebo, nothing in markets should follow it. Missing days (instrument outages) are left out. Observed flux varies about +-3.4% over the year with Earth-Sun distance (F10.7adj removes that). A few days exceed 500 sfu (e.g. 2001-12-28, 2003-11-04, 2005-09-09, 2006-12-06): solar radio bursts from major flares during the noon measurement, kept as published.

name: International sunspot number, daily total (v2.0)
notes: PLACEBO: no plausible mechanism links sunspots to next-day US stock moves; a lead-lag hit here measures the test's false-positive rate. Can be 0 at solar minimum, hence diff. Values from 2026-07-01 on are provisional (definitive flag 0). The whole series was recalibrated (v2.0) in July 2015, so pre-2015 values differ from what was published then (a scale change, harmless for correlation). Daily values before 1849 are sparse; missing (-1) left out. SILSO updates this file monthly; the next-day estimate (EISN) is published daily.
